trustBoundaries.description: Flutter/Dart application code, bundled resources, and runtime memory on a user-controlled device
SharedPreferences and application-support files on the local device
Third-party Google Mobile Ads SDK and its network endpoints
Approved CI/external secret store for future signing and release credentials
Future first-party backend boundary; no backend is currently integrated

networkPolicy.certificatePinningRationale: No first-party authenticated backend exists yet; revisit when one is introduced.
futureBackendRules: no reusable privileged secret embedded in the client
privacy inventory update before enabling new data flows

threats.scenario: Attacker decompiles or inspects APK/AAB/IPA resources and Dart/native code to recover configuration or logic.
mitigations: Treat all shipped client configuration as public
Never embed reusable privileged secrets
Inject signing/service credentials only from approved secret stores
threats.residualRisk: Game logic and public identifiers remain inspectable by design.

threats.scenario: User or malware alters SharedPreferences/local files to change coins, progress, boosters, settings, or diagnostics.
mitigations: Validate and clamp persisted values on load
Keep economy/progression mutations bounded and tested
Do not treat client-side values as authoritative for future server rewards
threats.residualRisk: Offline single-player progress can be modified on rooted/jailbroken devices.

threats.scenario: Attacker modifies and redistributes a repackaged build or hooks runtime behavior.
mitigations: Release signing keys remain outside source control
Official distribution relies on platform signature verification
No client-side integrity check is treated as an authorization boundary
threats.residualRisk: Unofficial modified builds remain possible outside trusted distribution channels.

threats.scenario: Network attacker observes or modifies traffic to third-party or future first-party services.
mitigations: Require TLS for declared network communication
Disallow application cleartext traffic
Use scoped/expiring tokens for any future authenticated backend
threats.residualRisk: Third-party SDK endpoint security remains partly controlled by the processor/platform.

threats.scenario: Credentials leak through source, build config, logs, screenshots, diagnostics, CI output, or artifacts.
mitigations: Repository secret-hygiene CI guard
SecretRedactor before diagnostic persistence/copy
No signing/private credentials in Dart defines or source
Rotation required after suspected exposure
threats.residualRisk: Unknown credential formats may evade pattern-based redaction; callers must avoid logging secrets.

threats.scenario: Runtime errors expose tokens, user-specific paths, private keys, or sensitive context.
mitigations: Central redaction before memory/file/debug/clipboard/runtime broadcasts
Diagnostics remain local-only in the current product
Privacy inventory and future crash reporting require explicit gates
threats.residualRisk: Unexpected sensitive formats may appear in third-party exception text.

threats.scenario: A Flutter/native dependency introduces vulnerable code, unexpected data collection, or malicious build behavior.
mitigations: Dependencies remain explicit in pubspec and lockfile
Privacy inventory blocks selected unreviewed analytics/cloud SDK additions
Secret and asset CI guards run before build
threats.residualRisk: Automated vulnerability/license scanning is not yet complete.

threats.scenario: Malformed persisted values, asset metadata, route actions, or repeated UI events produce crashes or duplicate state mutation.
mitigations: Typed asset/config registries validate inputs
ProgressStore clamps and validates economy/progression values
Navigation and gameplay actions use duplicate/race guards
Missing/corrupt assets have bounded fallbacks
threats.residualRisk: Future external/deep-link inputs require dedicated validation as they are introduced.

threats.scenario: Advertising SDK processing occurs without required consent or is mistaken for first-party offline behavior.
mitigations: Ads can be disabled globally by build configuration
Google Mobile Ads is explicitly declared in privacy inventory
Production consent remains a blocking ADS-007 responsibility
threats.residualRisk: Production consent and regional behavior are not complete until ADS-007 is verified.
